subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend seam, and should the first implementation bridge to Gateway `tools.media.audio` under explicit credential, private-network, and fallback policy?
rationale: Source proves the capability is missing, but implementation changes native app behavior, provider routing, microphone-audio handling, endpoint trust, and fallback semantics that automation should not choose.

options.title: Design Gateway-backed batch PTT seam
options.body: Add a maintainer-scoped native PTT backend abstraction that keeps Apple Speech as default and uses existing media/provider request controls for configured batch STT.

options.title: Defer native backend selection
options.body: Keep native PTT on Apple Speech until the broader native ASR plan across PTT, Talk, wake-word, and mobile surfaces is settled.

options.title: Route outside native capture
options.body: Treat sidecars, plugins, or existing provider paths as sufficient and avoid adding a native PTT backend seam for now.

recommendation.title: Design Gateway-backed batch PTT seam
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-scoped native PTT backend abstraction that keeps Apple Speech as default and uses existing media/provider request controls for configured batch STT.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current code-history signal is in native macOS PTT and adjacent voice/Talk files, where `steipete` is the clearest routing candidate.
